avatar.name: The Vanishing Identity Mother
avatar.description: A 31-year-old first-time mother at 4 months postpartum who feels like her youth, femininity, and bodily integrity are slipping down the bathroom drain in thick, tangled clumps every single shower.
avatar.awareness_notes: Problem-aware: she knows she is shedding heavily from postpartum hormone shifts, but falsely believes only biotin or waiting it out are her options.

pain_points.description: Standing in the shower with wet hands covered in long strands, terrified to run fingers through her hair because another clump will inevitably pull away.
examples: I looked down at my hands and there was a literal bird's nest of hair stuck to my palms.
I cry every single time I wash my hair now.
pain_points.label: PLAUSIBLE_INFERENCE

pain_points.description: Catching her reflection in the rearview mirror or under harsh bathroom lighting and seeing stark white scalp shining through widening temples.
examples: I can't put my hair up in a messy bun anymore because my hairline looks receded like an old man's.
I caught a glimpse of my scalp under the kitchen spotlights and felt completely sick.
pain_points.label: PLAUSIBLE_INFERENCE

pain_points.description: Feeling unattractive to her partner, constantly wearing headbands, and apologizing when her shed hairs are found on his shirts, bedsheets, and the baby's onesies.
examples: I pull my shed hairs off my baby's fingers and off my husband's chest and I just feel disgusting.
I don't want him to touch my head or run his fingers through my hair.
pain_points.label: PLAUSIBLE_INFERENCE

failed_attempts.attempt: The 'It's Just Hormones / Wait It Out' medical brush-off

Shame over loose hairs on baby clothes
future_fears: Permanent hairline recession that never recovers
Losing all feminine sex appeal and being seen only as a worn-out caretaker

product_fit.how_it_resolves: Directly halts the telogen detachment signal at the root within 14 days and triggers dense baby-hair regrowth along widened temples without systemic hormone disruption.
